uncited: Geometric and Structural Regularization imposes constraints on the learned radiance field to enforce physical plausibility, semantic consistency, or structural integrity, addressing the ambiguity inherent in sparse or ill-posed inverse volume rendering problems.

Unlike sibling methods that focus on pixel-level fidelity [10377-nerf-xl-multi-gpu-distortion-loss.md] or final loss aggregation [15455-final-loss-function.md], this family explicitly shapes the density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ fields using auxiliary objectives such as depth consistency, perceptual similarity, or semantic disentanglement.
It aims to correct the bias inherent in standard volume rendering by enforcing a more accurate distribution of weights along the ray.

Geometric and structural regularization evolved from the observation that standard NeRF training, relying solely on photometric loss, often produces artifacts in sparse-view settings or fails to capture fine semantic details.
These methods address the "slushy" appearance and lack of structural coherence in baseline NeRFs by injecting domain-specific knowledge into the optimization loop.
